scenes.headline: How one small head reads text, pictures, sound and video
scenes.sub: Jev-Omni: Gemma 4, a fine-tuned decoder and a 256-way head.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Peanut! Jev-Omni picks an option from text, images, audio or video, all through one small head.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: Pictures and sound become tokens through one small linear layer each, one decoder reads everything, and a 256-way head picks the answer.
scenes.say: Pictures and sound become tokens through one linear layer each. One decoder reads everything, and a small head picks the answer.

scenes.title: Four inputs, one decoder, one head

steps.say: Gemma 4 has no vision tower or audio encoder. A flat square of pixels, or a slice of raw samples, goes through one linear layer.
Those tokens join the text prompt, options numbered, in one decoder. The decoder was fine-tuned; the front end is Google's, untouched.
A head reads the last position: one linear layer to two hundred and fifty-six classes, with the unused classes masked away.

scenes.label: parameters in the whole non-text front end: 0.44% of the decoder
scenes.say: That whole front end is fifty-two million parameters, zero point four four percent of the decoder.

scenes.title: The option count is in the weights

left.title: Per-option scorer
items: Scores each option on its own
The option set is just data
left.say: A per-option scorer rates each option on its own, so the list is just data and the order can't matter.

right.title: Jev-Omni's 256-way head
items: Class i is list position i
So order can matter: reasoned, untested
right.say: Here, class one is whatever comes first in the list, and the count is welded into the weights. So order can matter. That's reasoned, not yet tested.

scenes.title: Median latency on an H200
scenes.note: the claim that travelled: under 100 ms on 1 H100
scenes.say: Per the card, text, image and audio land under a hundred milliseconds. Sixteen frames of video take five hundred and four.

scenes.title: The release's own headline chart
scenes.credit: the Jev-Omni release's own chart; the author's benchmark

steps.say: The release's own chart: Jev-Omni at eighty-seven point five seven, Jev at ninety point four eight. Below, not on par.
Three chat models sit eleven points above both. The chart's real argument is the bottom axis: cost.

scenes.text: Four modalities reach one head because the base model already turns them all into tokens. The decision training was text-decoder training.
scenes.mark: already turns them all into tokens
scenes.say: Four modalities reach one head because the base model already turns them all into tokens. The decision training was text training.

recap: Pixels and samples enter through one Linear each
One fine-tuned decoder reads every modality
A 256-way head with the option count welded in
scenes.say: To recap: tiny linear front ends, one fine-tuned decoder, and the option count in the head's weights.
